A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same FIXLIP research, with corresponding main sections, Tables 1–4, Figures 1–17, and Appendices A–E. The text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original explanation experiments on MS COCO and ImageNet-1k, including faithfulness, pointing-game recognition, computational timing, and qualitative model comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the numerical comparisons in Tables 1, 2, and 4 and Figures 3–5 and 10–12.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B.1 retain the weighted Banzhaf objective, p-weighted masking, cross-modal estimator, interaction filtering, and greedy subset selection. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MS COCO image–text pairs and ImageNet-1k-derived pointing games with the same object combinations and one-to-four-object scenarios. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership within the experiments is unchanged. XCLIP is renamed exCLIP, retaining the same underlying cited work, implementation link, and results. Its exclusion from the CLIP ViT-B/16 MS COCO comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The model variants, data splits, metrics, approximation budgets, and evaluation procedures are retained. Appendix C.2 clarifies 50 images per pointing-game scenario, consistent with the existing construction and 500-input reporting in Section 5.2; this does not establish a changed sample size.

E4.justification: The masking-weight sensitivity analyses, evaluation under different mask distributions, empty-input check, and qualitative token-conditioning and model-comparison examples are retained in Appendices B, D, and E. No additional analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain means with standard deviations across inputs and the same boxplot reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, performance plots, timing comparison, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Figure 3 reports AID scores of 1.02 ± 0.18 for FIXLIP p = 0.5 and 0.25 ± 0.18 for XCLIP/exCLIP in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, first-order conversion theorem, cross-modal estimator unbiasedness and variance bounds, and insertion/deletion proposition are unchanged. Appendix A retains the corresponding proofs, with only wording or typesetting differences.

C1.justification: The central claims about faithful interaction explanations, efficient computation, extended evaluation metrics, and model comparisons are retained. Removing the ViT-size comparison example from the abstract does not change the contribution’s scope; that comparison remains in Table 2.

C2.justification: The interpretations of masking-weight effects, baseline behavior, model differences, and the limitations in Section 6 are retained. Appendix E.2 adds literature context for the existing text-in-image examples without a substantive new mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a FIXLIP repository link and states that code reproducing all experiments is available, on the first page and in Section 6. Appendix C.2 clarifies 50 images per scenario, while C.5 revises total reported compute time from about 16 to 15 days.

R1.justification: Four references are added: hierarchical Banzhaf interaction for video–language learning, Parcalabescu and Frank’s 2025 decoder study, SceneTAP, and FigStep. Section 2 and Appendix E.2 gain limited context while retaining the existing research positioning. The exCLIP citation updates the publication information of an existing reference.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar and wording edits, renames XCLIP to exCLIP, updates affiliation and funding text, shortens the appendix heading, and adds a code paragraph. The section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Baseline labels change to exCLIP in figures and tables, and several captions receive light edits. The conference footer, code line, and text reflow alter page layout, while the figure/table inventory, structures, and visual evidence remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility documentation through an explicit experiment-code link and clearer pointing-game sample counts, with modest improvements to literature coverage and wording. The method, theory, and empirical support remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
